articles.title: How the 30-day savings rule can help you stop impulse spending and save more money
articles.summary: The 30-day savings rule is a simple strategy that helps you avoid overspending and get closer to reaching your savings goals. Here's how it works.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

If you struggle with impulsive spending, there's a strategy that may help. It's called the 30-day savings rule — a budgeting strategy designed to curb impulse spending and help you save more money. Here's how it works.

The 30-day savings rule is a simple strategy to cut down on overspending. It works like this: When you're tempted to make an impulse purchase, you commit to waiting 30 days before going through with it.

Of course, at the end of those 30 days, you may decide that you do, in fact, want to make the purchase. The 30-day rule isn't necessarily going to stop you from spending money completely. But it will force you to slow down, be more mindful about your purchases, and prevent you from buying items that you don't really need or want.

Extra time can give you the perspective you need to determine whether or not your purchase is necessary. It can also give you a chance to comparison shop, dig for coupons, or wait for the item to go on sale.

Pros and cons of the 30-day savings rule

Overall, you'll probably find that the 30-day savings rule has a positive impact on your finances. However, there are some drawbacks to consider, too.

Reduces impulse spending: Waiting 30 days gives you time to consider whether you truly need or want something rather than making an emotional or spontaneous purchase.

Helps you save money: By avoiding unnecessary purchases, you can free up money to put toward your emergency fund, retirement savings, debt repayment, or other financial goals.

Prevents buyer's remorse: Giving yourself time to think before making a purchase can reduce the likelihood of regretting it later.

Easy to implement: Unlike some budgeting strategies, the 30-day rule doesn't require complicated calculations, special apps, or tracking every dollar you spend.

Helps identify spending patterns: Keeping a list of purchases you're considering can reveal which types of products or experiences tend to trigger impulse spending.

Not always practical for certain purchases: Waiting 30 days isn't realistic when you need to replace a broken appliance, purchase necessary clothing, or cover another urgent expense.

You could miss out on legitimate savings: Delaying a purchase could mean missing a limited-time sale or promotional offer. But remember that a special deal only saves you money if you were already planning to buy the item in the first place.

Doesn't guarantee you'll save money: Simply postponing purchases won't necessarily improve your finances if you eventually buy everything on your list. To maximize your savings, consider transferring the money you would have spent on unwanted purchases into a savings account.

Can feel overly restrictive: Waiting an entire month for every discretionary purchase may feel frustrating, especially if you have enough room in your budget to comfortably afford smaller purchases.

How much money can the 30-day savings rule save you?

Sure, a last-minute pack of gum at the register may not put a dent in your budget. But impulsive spending can add up, especially if you're not taking the time to think through more expensive purchases.

According to research by Capital One Shopping , the average consumer spends $254 per month on impulse buys, for an annual total of $3,045. That's money that could be put toward paying off debt, building an emergency fund, or even funding a vacation.

For example, say you take that $254 and deposit it into a high-yield savings account each month instead of spending it. If your account earns 4% APY, you'd make an extra $57 in interest over the course of the year. Plus, you'd end up with more than $3,000 set aside as a safety net, which can go a long way toward improving your financial well-being .

Of course, your personal spending habits will dictate how much you can save by implementing this rule. But even small changes can have a positive impact on your finances.

How to implement the 30-day savings rule

Let's say you're shopping, and an item catches your eye that wasn't actually on your shopping list — or even on your radar until this very moment. Before you commit to the purchase, open up your phone and make a note of the item, along with where it can be purchased, the price information, and any relevant links (if it's online).

Then leave the item and plan to revisit that note in 30 days. In the meantime, ask yourself a few key questions:

How would this purchase impact my budget and savings goals?

First, it's important to consider whether you can truly afford the purchase. You should have enough disposable income to cover the cost without impacting your short-term budget or long-term goals.

Can I get this item for a lower price somewhere else?

Comparison shopping is a great way to save, but it isn't possible when you make a purchase impulsively. By adopting the 30-day rule, you give yourself enough time to browse online and hit a few different stores to see if the item you want is available for a lower price somewhere else.

Are there any upcoming sales or discounts?

Do some research to see if the particular store you're shopping with has an upcoming sale or if there's a coupon available that can help you save.

Maybe there's a similar or off-brand version that doesn't cost as much. It can be easy to get swayed by high-end labels sometimes, but there are often generic alternatives to most items that cost a fraction of the price for the same end result.

How many hours would I have to work to pay for this item?

Thinking about purchases in terms of your time can help put things into perspective. For example, if something costs $100 and you have the money to pay for it, you may not think twice. But what if, instead, you thought about pricing in terms of how long you would need to work to earn that money? Say you earn $15 per hour — six hours of work to pay for an impulse buy may not seem worth it after all.

When faced with the opportunity to buy something that catches your eye, it can be hard to say no — especially if you have the money in your bank account to cover the splurge.

However, giving yourself time and space from an unplanned purchase might actually help you decide if you need it or if it was just a momentary lapse in judgment. Depending on the price tag, taking this pause can save you from derailing your budget.

articles.title: Trump bought Nvidia shares, then cleared path for chip sales to China: Report
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump bought millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares before taking decisions that eased restrictions on the chipmaker's exports to
articles.body: US President Donald Trump bought millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares before taking decisions that eased restrictions on the chipmaker's exports to China, an analysis of his financial disclosures has found.According to an analysis by anti-corruption group DeKleptocracy, Trump's disclosures show he purchased between $1 million and $5 million worth of Nvidia stock in the days before his administration scrapped a Biden-era export rule in May 2025.The rule, known as the diffusion rule, was intended to restrict exports of advanced US-made artificial intelligence (AI) chips to China over concerns that Beijing could use the technology to develop superior AI capabilities. Its removal opened the way for Nvidia to expand sales in a market that accounted for about a quarter of its revenue between 2010 and 2022.Nvidia shares rose in value after Trump announced the reversal. His disclosures also showed purchases of shares in other technology companies, including Apple, Meta and Microsoft.The president's Nvidia investments continued as his administration moved to ease restrictions further. In December 2025, Trump announced that Nvidia would be allowed to sell its H200 chips to China. The US commerce department approved the move in January 2026.The decision drew criticism over the potential implications for US national security. Experts said the H200 chips were among Nvidia's most advanced products and were six times more powerful than the chips available in China at the time, the Guardian reported.The council on foreign relations warned that their sale could “supercharge” China's future AI factories and strengthen the US's rival.Trump's financial disclosures indicate that he made at least three Nvidia stock purchases in the days after announcing the H200 decision. Each transaction was valued between $250,001 and $500,000. He appears to have made dozens of Nvidia-related stock transactions since taking office, with some ranking among his largest purchases.The stock purchases have come amid separate scrutiny of Nvidia's links to an alleged Chinese intelligence operation. Reports have alleged that Alice Huang, described as a Chinese spy, had an affair with Nvidia's former chief executive Jensen Huang, and that her company, Megaspeed, obtained billions of dollars' worth of the chipmaker's products.Trump was briefed twice by US intelligence officials on their assessment that Alice Huang was a Chinese asset, but did not act on it, according to The Guardian.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Anthropic IPO to test Wall Street's faith in AI as skepticism mounts
articles.summary: Anthropic seeks a valuation of approximately $1.3 trillion to $1.4 trillion.
articles.body:
There were no rockets decking Wall Street bank lobbies this past week, unlike the spectacle surrounding SpaceX's blockbuster June listing.

Instead, bankers marketing Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) potentially record-breaking initial public offering this week faced an unusually turbulent backdrop as Treasury yields surged and a widespread Microsoft Outlook outage hampered communications, all during — the biggest disruption of all — the sudden ousting of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang, whose company is among Anthropic's biggest investors and chip suppliers.

At a JPMorgan Chase investor event Friday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei outlined a future in which AI could help make diseases such as cancer and Alzheimer's relics of the past, while devising entirely new markets in scientific research, robotics, and cybersecurity.

"We can have a much more beautiful world ... It sounds starry-eyed. It sounds crazy. I really do believe it," Amodei told JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon.

Yet Amodei struck a more restrained tone about the company's move to go public, saying he hopes the company will "underpromise and overdeliver."

"We're not super fussed on when exactly, what month or what day or what market conditions we go public into," he added.

The comments come as Anthropic seeks a valuation of approximately $1.3 trillion to $1.4 trillion, below the $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion figures investors had contemplated just weeks earlier.

The offering, expected to begin trading on Thursday, Nov. 19, could provide one of the clearest tests yet of investors' appetite for AI at a moment when enthusiasm for the broader trade is showing signs of cracks.

The contrast between Anthropic's lofty ambitions and Amodei's measured approach to the IPO has also been apparent in Wall Street's marketing campaign.

The lobbies of JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, and Goldman Sachs have been decorated to welcome the startup, according to people familiar with the arrangements. But the displays are more subdued than the digital displays and skyscraper illuminations of rocket ships Wall Street bank visitors witnessed during SpaceX's June IPO, or the meteorite exhibit at JPMorgan's Manhattan headquarters.

Banks are nevertheless mounting a substantial effort to attract investors.

At Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, the two banks leading the offering, Anthropic executives met with institutional investors earlier this week. Goldman is also planning an event next week for wealth management clients, where the bank's president, John Waldron, is expected to interview Anthropic president Daniela Amodei and CFO Krishna Rao, according to a people familiar with the plans.

articles.title: AMD Just Had Its Biggest Run Against Nvidia Since 1999. Can It Survive Earnings?
articles.summary: AMD stock beat Nvidia by a record margin over 5 days, then fell 8.75% with Nvidia's first post-Huang earnings due November 17.
articles.body:
AMD outperformed Nvidia by 53.2 percentage points over five trading days, according to The Kobeissi Letter. That is the widest gap between the two chipmakers since Nvidia went public in January 1999.

That lead met its first test on Friday, when AMD stock fell 8.75%. Nvidia's November 17 earnings report now sets up the next one.

How Nvidia's Leadership Crisis Fed the AMD Rally

AMD rallied 44.7% over the 5-day stretch while Nvidia dropped 8.5%, according to The Kobeissi Letter. The previous record gap, set in April 2016, stood at 49.9 percentage points.

So far this year, the AMD vs Nvidia gap is even wider. AMD stock has gained 149.4% since January 1, while Nvidia is down 12.7%, as of Friday's close. That puts the year-to-date gap at about 162 percentage points.

The run overlapped with growing scrutiny of Jensen Huang, who quit Nvidia as CEO on November 12. The company named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent replacement.

AMD also gave buyers its own numbers to work with. Its third-quarter revenue rose 45% from a year earlier to a record $13.4 billion. Data center sales nearly doubled to $8.5 billion.

"AMD has been a major beneficiary of Nvidia's historic volatility," The Kobeissi Letter posted on X.

Friday's Sell-Off Hands the Next Move to Nvidia

The record run lost some ground in Friday's session. AMD closed at $534.06, down from $585.30, and slipped another 2.41% to $521.20 after hours.

Chip stocks sold off as a group. The 10-year Treasury yield remained above 5% after October's producer price index. Rising yields tend to hit growth stocks hardest, since their value rests on profits expected years ahead.

Trading volume reached 48.6 million shares, nearly double the 3-month average. Analysts at The Motley Fool linked part of the drop to profit-taking after the surge.

The after-hours price now sits just above $514. BeInCrypto's AMD stock price analysis marked that level as the line that would break the bullish setup.

Nvidia earnings land on Tuesday after the US market closes. The company guided for $108 billion in third-quarter revenue, plus or minus 2%. Analysts polled by LSEG expect about $109.2 billion and adjusted earnings of $2.48 per share.

The quarter closed on October 25, before Huang resigned, so the results will reflect his tenure. The guidance for the next quarter will be the first issued with Kress as interim CEO.

Solid results and guidance could draw investors back to Nvidia. A weak one could drag the whole chip group lower, AMD included, because Friday showed both stocks still trade together.

articles.title: A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO has over 100,000 signatures, including some big names
articles.summary: Organizers of the petition say some 50,000 shareholders and 5,000 current Nvidia employees, have signed their petition to bring back Jensen Huang.
articles.body:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after admitting to an affair.

Nvidia is investigating whether the affair was a "foreign intelligence effort."

Over 100,000 people have now signed a petition to reinstate Huang, including Elon Musk and others.

Some people aren't ready to let former CEO Jensen Huang go.

A petition to reinstate Huang as Nvidia's CEO has over 108,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon, including prominent tech leaders such as billionaire Elon Musk and Replit CEO Amjad Masad. Both executives promoted the petition on X.

A website for the campaign, dubbed "Stand with Jensen," said the list includes more than 58,000 shareholders, more than 5,600 current Nvidia employees, and over 1,000 former employees.

It also, to be fair, included "Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor" and "Xi Jingping," a possibly misspelled reference to the Chinese leader. In an X post on Saturday, the organizers said they were "actively working" to remove fake signatures.

One Nvidia employee who signed the letter told Business Insider that similar efforts are happening inside the company. A post with similar sentiments appeared on an internal portal where employees can submit questions and suggestions, they said.

Wired reported that the post had garnered 1,600 comments as of Thursday — a figure that has now more than doubled, the employee said.

Earlier this week, Nvidia's board of directors said it opened an investigation into whether Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort" after he admitted to having an affair in a letter to staffers. Days later, Huang resigned after reports he had another affair with an Nvidia executive, and the board appointed Colette Kress , executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO until they find a permanent successor.

An October report by The New York Times said Huang had developed a "close relationship" with Alice Huang , a tech executive at Megaspeed in Singapore. The Times reported that US intelligence officials said she may be a spy for the Chinese government. China has since denied that claim. On Thursday, Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Department of Justice had not concluded whether Alice Huang was a spy.

The "Stand with Jensen" organizers said in an open letter to Nvidia's board posted to its website that they believe the board removed Huang without an investigation and "meaningful due process."

"We have not been shown evidence substantiating the espionage allegation. After thirty-three years pouring his heart and soul into NVIDIA, Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice," they said.

articles.title: Why Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan has 22 meetings a day — and what you can learn from it
articles.summary: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan is a tech warrior. Learn from him.
articles.body:
If you want to get ahead in business, sometimes you have to set aside the concept of having an amazing work-life balance.

Leaders at the highest levels of corporate America have told me repeatedly that work-life balance is great in theory, but it doesn't exist if you want to get big things done. They say you have to win every second, every minute, every hour, and every day to get ahead.

Take Intel ( INTC ) CEO Lip-Bu Tan as an example. More than a year into the top job at Intel, the tech veteran and former basketball player is having grueling days at 66 that most 21-year-olds couldn't keep up with. For Tan, maximizing time is of the essence in trying to turn around the iconic Intel.

"I broke my own record. I had 22 meetings a day for the first few months [on the job], and because time is not on my side," Tan said at Yahoo Finance Invest this week.

Under Tan's leadership, Intel has won deserved praise on Wall Street. The company's execution and competitiveness in its core client and data center compute markets have improved. Next-generation manufacturing execution has steadied, notably yields, manufacturability, foundry process, and advanced packaging.

These are all metrics foundational to the Intel comeback story, and the Street tracks them like a hawk.

The company did have a stumble recently, however, with its third quarter earnings report.

The stock collapsed after Intel's forecast for fourth quarter sales fell well shy of expectations due to a worse-than-expected decline in PC sales. At the center of the PC weakness is a shortage of memory chips, which are being snapped up by AI hyperscalers, pushing prices up and causing consumers to delay purchases.

At the same time, an explosion at Intel's Kiryat Gat chip fabrication facility in Israel in early October will cost the company about $600 million in lost sales across two quarters, the company said. The lost sales include 10-nanometer server shipments.

Why the biggest risk for investors in 2027 isn't Nvidia — it's inflation

From SpaceX's IPO to orbital data centers, execs say industry's future still in 'earliest innings'

Bill Ackman says Microsoft's position is 'really, really strong' as Anthropic pushes into enterprise software

Intel stock is down 42% over the past month.

Tan said he is having fewer meetings each day, but still has the engineering team report directly to him. His daily schedule is a masterclass in scheduling, interspersed with strategic moments to reset and recover.

"My routine is very simple, and it depends on what day and what time the first meeting is," Tan said. "I usually have swimming and the gym. I usually take about one hour, and so if the meeting starts at seven, then I wake up at 5:30 a.m., and then I go to swim and the gym, and that's also my time of meditation. Then I start my days either with a conference call or physical meeting. My day usually is long until almost 1 o'clock in the morning, … so that is kind of a lot of meetings, a lot of phone calls, and a lot of get-togethers. Then the weekend usually is my more effective time, so that's where I deep dive with my team, deep dive with some of the areas I want to focus, and then so Saturday and Sunday usually I am kind of tied up."

articles.title: Strong economy drives NH toll to record 6,640cr in Oct
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Toll collection on national highways and expressways touched an all-time high of around Rs 6,640 crore in Oct, indicating stronger economic
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Toll collection on national highways and expressways touched an all-time high of around Rs 6,640 crore in Oct, indicating stronger economic activity and increased movement of vehicles across the country's highway network.The collection of user fee was around 16% higher than the Rs 5,715 crore recorded in Oct 2025. The previous highest monthly toll revenue was Rs 6,185 crore, collected in May this year. Going by the trend, the total toll collection is projected to be around Rs 74,000 crore, officials said.A significant change was also visible in the mode of payment, with cash collections dropping sharply to barely Rs 4 crore last month from Rs 84 crore in the corresponding month last year. At the same time, payments through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) rose to around Rs 100 crore in Oct, against no such collection a year ago.The sharp decline in cash transactions follows govt directions to move away from cash payments for highway user fees and use FASTag or UPI as the default modes for paying the user charge. Officials said stricter monitoring was being carried out to ensure that cash is completely phased out as a mode of toll payment. "End of cash transaction will eliminate any scope of malpractices. More people are also opting for FASTag Annual Passes, which is a good sign," said another official. Growing adoption of electronic toll collection has reduced dependence on cash at toll plazas. The rise in UPI payments also indicates the gradual expansion of digital payment options for highway users.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: US trade deal talks near finishing line: EAM
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar Saturday said many of the pending issues in the trade deal with the US were \"not so much at our end\" and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar Saturday said many of the pending issues in the trade deal with the US were "not so much at our end" and that negotiations are near the "finishing line"."Well, it's certainly our hope, and in many ways anticipation that we are at the last stretch," he said.The comments come a week after a team of US officials came to India to discuss the customs and trade facilitation chapter with India, which is waiting for clarity on what the new tariff framework will be after the US Supreme Court ruled that US President Donald Trump's "reciprocal tariffs" were illegal. His comments may be an indication that govt is awaiting the next step from the Trump administration - which is conducting a second Section 301 probe against over a dozen countries for structural overcapacity.For several weeks now, officials from both sides have been stating that talks are in the final lap, with Trump also saying the deal with India may be different from other deals. "For us, the key is that we want a trade deal which is beneficial, is balanced and which would give us a comparative advantage over groups of comparable economies," Jaishankar said at the HT Leadership Summit.The repeated comments have raised hopes of the first tranche of the deal being announced soon, although things can move only after the US Trade Representative completes the second probe. PM Modi and Trump are due to meet in the US next month.Jaishankar said the US is India's biggest market and having the trade deal with it would benefit the country. "For the US, Trump is obviously looking to do a whole set of bilateral deals to improve markets for himself. Now, the challenge is to find a landing point.""I think this is not something which could have been done quickly, because these are serious issues; people's jobs and people's lives are at stake."Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Online platforms liable for banned listings: Panel
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An online platform cannot hide behind its intermediary status to evade responsibility under consumer protection law and must exercise due
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An online platform cannot hide behind its intermediary status to evade responsibility under consumer protection law and must exercise due diligence before allowing listings of prohibited, hazardous and regulated products, the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) has ruled.The order will have wider implications and act as a deterrent to the sale of hazardous items such as explosives, acids and jammers that pose a danger, as well as other regulated products. Online platforms and e-commerce companies often cite their intermediary status to escape responsibility and action in such cases.The NCDRC passed the order while hearing appeals filed by Weblink.in against two orders of the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) concerning the online listing of ammonium nitrate, picric acid and pentaerythritol tetranitrate. The authority had imposed a penalty of Rs 20 lakh on the platform in the two cases.The commission upheld the penalty imposed by the authority. In its order passed earlier this week, the commission said the platform could not claim immunity under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act on the ground that it had no “actual knowledge” of the listings. It also said the company could not plead “selective diligence”.In one of the orders, the commission said, “The platform has its own list of do’s and don’ts, and it is evident they are not unaware of the precautions while facilitating transactions through their platforms in respect of hazardous substances or such prohibited items detrimental to the life of consumers. The argument that they are not obliged to verify licences as there is no such statutory obligation deserves rejection as the platform has the obligation to take reasonable care and exercise due diligence while allowing its platform to be utilised for such advertisement...”Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Megaspeed Malaysian arm Speedmatrix under scanner
articles.summary: Kuala Lumpur: The spotlight is now on Malaysia as the fallout of the Nvidia spy scandal engulfs more companies and alleged South East Asia-based
articles.body: Kuala Lumpur: The spotlight is now on Malaysia as the fallout of the Nvidia spy scandal engulfs more companies and alleged South East Asia-based intermediaries. Fears of high-performance Nvidia chips finding their way to China through Malaysia, bypassing the US trade curbs, have swung the authorities here into action.Ministry of investment, trade and industry (MITI) has intensified the probe into Speedmatrix Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte Ltd, in collaboration with Royal Malaysian Customs Department.Malaysia's home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said on Saturday that police had opened an investigation paper as early as April 2025 on allegations that Malaysian subsidiaries were used to circumvent US export restrictions on Nvidia AI chips.In a statement on Friday, MITI said emphatically that "it has never cleared Singapore-based Megaspeed or its Malaysian affiliate Speedmatrix.""Speedmatrix is a tenant at data centres in Malaysia. Any verification visits carried out by MITI at these facilities are part of its regular monitoring of the data center sector, and should not be taken to mean that a company has been cleared. Any suggestion otherwise is inaccurate," MITI stated.So what prompted MITI to take this stance when only a few days ago minister Johari Abdul Ghani said govt has not opened a formal inquiry into Speedmatrix as there was no evidence the firm broke the law by renting data centre space and using GPUs locally?Two things unfolded: Megaspeed's claims that inspections by US and Malaysian officials found no foul play, implying the company stayed in line, and second, industry sources said, the realisation that Malaysia's recent pivot to AI hardware, chip design and a strong data centre hub could possibly be hit if a rules-based ecosystem was missing from the narrative.Money habits form by age 7.
